articles.title: Vereador de Paranatama morre após ser atropelado na BR-423 | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima foi o parlamentar Josemar Luiz de Melo, conhecido na cidade por Josa Moita, de 63 anos. Causas do acidente não foram divulgadas pela polícia.
articles.summary: Vítima foi o parlamentar Josemar Luiz de Melo, conhecido na cidade por Josa Moita, de 63 anos. Causas do acidente não foram divulgadas pela polícia.
articles.body:
Josa Moita, vereador de Paranatama, morre após ser atropelado na BR-423 — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Um vereador de Paranatama , no Agreste de Pernambuco, morreu após não resistir aos ferimentos provocados por um atropelamento na BR-423. O acidente aconteceu no último sábado (29), próximo a um posto de combustível do município. As causas do acidente não foram divulgadas. A vítima foi o parlamentar Josemar Luiz de Melo, conhecido na cidade por Josa Moita, de 63 anos.

Após ser atropelado, o vereador foi socorrido e levado para o Hospital Regional Dom Moura, em Garanhuns . Devido à gravidade do quadro clínico, ele foi transferido para o Hospital da Restauração, no Recife. O falecimento aconteceu na madrugada desta segunda-feira (31).

Por meio das redes sociais, a prefeitura de Paranatama emitiu uma nota de pesar lamentando o falecimento do vereador Josa Mota. “Neste momento de dor e consternação, expressamos nossas mais sinceras condolências aos familiares, amigos e a todos que tiveram oportunidade de conviver com ele”.

A Câmara Municipal também decretou luto e se solidarizou com os familiares, amigos e toda a população.

“Em sua trajetória parlamentar, Josa Moita dedicou seu trabalho à defesa dos interesses da população de Paranatama, deixando sua contribuição para o município”, diz nota da Casa Legislativa.

Este era o quinto mandato de Josa como vereador. Ele foi reeleito nas eleições municipais de 2024 pelo partido Movimento Democrático Brasileiro (MDB) com 593 votos.

articles.title: Hospital Unimed Teresina completa 10 anos com trajetória marcada por cuidado e inovação | G1
articles.standfirst: Unidade consolidou-se como um dos principais pilares da rede própria da cooperativa, ampliando a oferta de serviços de alta complexidade e fortalecendo a assistência à saúde no Piauí.
articles.summary: Unidade consolidou-se como um dos principais pilares da rede própria da cooperativa, ampliando a oferta de serviços de alta complexidade e fortalecendo a assistência à saúde no Piauí.
articles.body:
Localizado no bairro Primavera, o Hospital Unimed consolidou-se como referência em alta complexidade, inovação e cuidado humanizado. — Foto: Unimed Teresina

Há dez anos, a Unimed Teresina inaugurava um dos principais projetos da sua história: o Hospital Unimed Teresina. Criado para ampliar a capacidade assistencial da cooperativa e oferecer aos beneficiários uma estrutura própria preparada para atendimentos de maior complexidade, o hospital transformou-se, ao longo dessa década, em um símbolo do compromisso da instituição com a qualidade, a inovação e o cuidado humanizado.

Inaugurado em 30 de agosto de 2016, o Hospital Unimed Teresina nasceu em um momento de expansão da saúde suplementar em Teresina, quando havia uma demanda crescente por serviços especializados, tecnologia médica e estruturas hospitalares capazes de oferecer maior resolutividade aos pacientes. A criação da unidade representou um novo capítulo para a cooperativa, fortalecendo sua rede própria e ampliando a capacidade de conduzir diferentes etapas do cuidado dentro da própria instituição.

“O Hospital Unimed tem uma importância histórica para a Unimed Teresina porque ele representa a consolidação de um projeto de fortalecimento da nossa rede própria. Quando pensamos na criação dessa unidade, tínhamos o objetivo de oferecer aos nossos beneficiários uma assistência cada vez mais completa, com estrutura, tecnologia e equipes preparadas para os desafios da medicina moderna. Hoje, ao olhar para esses dez anos, vemos uma instituição que cresceu, evoluiu e se tornou referência no cuidado à saúde no Piauí”, diz o presidente da Unimed Teresina, Dr. Rodrigo Pereira.

Desde sua inauguração, o hospital foi planejado para atuar como uma unidade de referência em alta complexidade. A estrutura inicial contava com 12 mil metros quadrados de área construída, 106 leitos, oito salas cirúrgicas, Unidade de Terapia Intensiva, Hemodinâmica e serviços especializados para atender pacientes que necessitavam de acompanhamento hospitalar diferenciado.

Ao longo dos anos, o Hospital Unimed passou por um processo contínuo de expansão física e assistencial. Novos serviços foram incorporados, equipamentos foram modernizados e equipes multiprofissionais foram fortalecidas, acompanhando a evolução da medicina e as novas necessidades dos pacientes.

Segundo o presidente da Unimed Teresina, o hospital continuará desempenhando papel fundamental no futuro da cooperativa. “A nossa visão é seguir avançando, investindo em inovação, qualificação profissional e novos modelos de cuidado. O Hospital Unimed Teresina tem uma trajetória construída no presente, mas com os olhos voltados para o futuro, buscando sempre oferecer uma assistência mais segura, eficiente e humanizada”, frisa Dr. Rodrigo.

Ao longo dessa década, a unidade ampliou sua capacidade e passou a oferecer uma estrutura cada vez mais completa, com pronto atendimento adulto 24 horas, centro cirúrgico, hemodinâmica, centro de infusão e oncologia, UTIs adulta e pediátrica, além de serviços de diagnóstico e tratamento especializados.

Evolução estrutural e assistencial consolida hospital como referência em Teresina

Para o superintendente de Recursos Próprios da Unimed Teresina, Hugo Neves, a história do Hospital Unimed Teresina é marcada por uma evolução constante, acompanhando o crescimento da demanda e os avanços da assistência hospitalar.

“A aquisição do hospital pela Unimed Teresina representou um marco na consolidação de um novo padrão de qualidade e assistência em saúde. Integrado à rede própria da cooperativa, o hospital possibilita a manutenção de uma estrutura alinhada às necessidades dos beneficiários, com investimentos contínuos, atendimento qualificado, resolutividade e indicadores assistenciais que reforçam seu papel como referência em saúde no estado”, pontua.

Segundo o gestor, o crescimento da unidade foi construído a partir de planejamento e investimento contínuo. “Cada ampliação, cada novo equipamento e cada serviço implantado tiveram como objetivo tornar o hospital mais resolutivo. Hoje temos uma estrutura preparada para atender casos de diferentes níveis de complexidade, com equipes especializadas e processos cada vez mais organizados.”

A trajetória da instituição de saúde também acompanha a evolução da medicina dentro da instituição. A incorporação de novos procedimentos e tecnologias permitiu que a unidade passasse a realizar atendimentos cada vez mais complexos, fortalecendo seu papel como referência regional.

Para o diretor técnico do Hospital Unimed Teresina, Dr. Jório Neiva, essa evolução está diretamente relacionada à qualificação das equipes e ao compromisso permanente com a segurança assistencial.

“Quando assumi a Diretoria Técnica, em março deste ano, encontrei um hospital consolidado em Teresina. Este recurso próprio da Unimed Teresina vem crescendo e evoluindo bastante, tanto em tecnologia quanto na capacidade de realizar procedimentos cada vez mais complexos. Um exemplo é sermos referência em transplante renal, com destaque também para o uso de técnicas minimamente invasivas, neuromonitorização e hemodinâmica”, frisa.

O diretor técnico destaca ainda que a segurança do paciente se tornou uma prioridade permanente. “Na jornada do paciente, o nosso Centro de Operações Logísticas Assistenciais – COLA – representa outro avanço importante. Hoje conseguimos acompanhar o hospital em tempo real, integrar diferentes áreas e apoiar decisões mais rápidas, contribuindo para melhorar o giro de leito e reduzir tempos de espera. Na Oncologia, o sistema ‘Atende Já’ também vem ajudando nessa jornada, com uma árvore de respostas automatizadas que agiliza o atendimento e direciona melhor o paciente”, diz.

Certificações reforçam compromisso com qualidade e segurança

A evolução do Hospital Unimed Teresina também é reconhecida por importantes conquistas relacionadas à qualidade assistencial. A unidade conquistou a Acreditação ONA Nível 1, concedida pela Organização Nacional de Acreditação, reconhecimento que avalia critérios relacionados à segurança do paciente, gestão dos processos e melhoria contínua.

O hospital também alcançou resultados de destaque na Avaliação Nacional das Práticas de Segurança do Paciente, realizada pela Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa), atingindo 100% de conformidade nos indicadores avaliados.

Esses resultados refletem uma construção coletiva envolvendo profissionais assistenciais, equipes administrativas e setores estratégicos, fortalecendo uma cultura organizacional baseada em qualidade, prevenção de riscos e aprimoramento permanente.

Além disso, a unidade passou a incorporar práticas voltadas à sustentabilidade e à governança, acompanhando uma visão moderna de gestão hospitalar. “Chegar aos 10 anos com esse nível de estrutura, tecnologia, segurança e, principalmente, com um corpo clínico cada vez mais engajado mostra que o hospital está em constante evolução. Mais do que construir um hospital de alta complexidade, estamos construindo uma forma cada vez melhor de cuidar das pessoas”, destaca o Dr. Jório.

Uma década de histórias, transformações e construção coletiva

Por trás da estrutura e dos indicadores, a história do Hospital Unimed Teresina também é formada pelas pessoas que participaram da sua construção desde os primeiros anos.

A gerente assistencial dos Recursos Próprios da Unimed Teresina, Angeline Andrade, que acompanha a trajetória da instituição desde o início, destaca as mudanças vivenciadas ao longo da década.

“Quando chegamos aos primeiros anos do hospital, havia uma grande expectativa sobre tudo que aquela estrutura representaria para a saúde do nosso Estado. Aos poucos, fomos construindo processos, fortalecendo equipes e aprendendo diariamente. É muito gratificante olhar para trás e perceber o quanto evoluímos”, lembra.

Segundo ela, uma das maiores transformações foi perceber a mudança na rotina assistencial. “A estrutura cresceu, os serviços aumentaram, a tecnologia avançou, mas algo permaneceu igual: o compromisso das pessoas em cuidar. São muitas histórias de pacientes, famílias e profissionais que fazem parte dessa trajetória.”

Para o diretor superintendente da Unimed Teresina, Dr. Raimundo Viana, o Hospital Unimed Teresina também representa uma conquista para a prática médica e para a relação entre cooperativa, médicos e assistência. “O hospital criou um ambiente onde os médicos cooperados puderam ampliar sua atuação, com uma estrutura moderna e preparada para acompanhar a evolução da medicina. Essa integração entre cooperativa, profissionais e hospital fortalece a assistência e beneficia diretamente o paciente”, pontua.

Ele ressalta ainda o impacto da evolução tecnológica. “A medicina mudou muito nesses últimos anos e o hospital acompanhou esse movimento. Investimos em equipamentos, processos e estrutura para que nossos médicos tenham condições adequadas de oferecer o melhor cuidado possível”, afirma

Ao completar dez anos, o Hospital Unimed celebra mais do que uma década de funcionamento. Celebra histórias, conquistas e uma trajetória construída por milhares de pessoas que fizeram da unidade um dos principais símbolos da Unimed Teresina.

A partir de uma estrutura criada para ampliar o acesso à assistência especializada, o hospital consolidou-se como referência em alta complexidade, inovação e cuidado humanizado, reafirmando o compromisso da cooperativa com um novo jeito de cuidar.

articles.title: Motorista morre após carro bater contra carreta e capotar na BR-163  | G1
articles.standfirst: Francisco Chagas, de 42 anos, morreu ainda no local do acidente. O condutor da carreta não se feriu.
articles.summary: Francisco Chagas, de 42 anos, morreu ainda no local do acidente. O condutor da carreta não se feriu.
articles.body:
Francisco Chagas, de 42 anos, morreu após sofrer um acidente de trânsito na BR-163 — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

O motorista Francisco Chagas, de 42 anos , morreu após o carro que ele conduzia bater contra o vagão de uma carreta no km 793 da BR-163, em Vera , a 459 km de Cuiabá, nesse domingo (31). Após a batida, o carro saiu da pista e capotou.

Segundo a Nova Rota do Oeste, concessionária de trânsito que administra o trecho, as informações preliminares apontam que Francisco perdeu o controle da direção do veículo e invadiu a pista contrária, momento em que o acidente ocorreu.

O resgate da Nova Rota esteve no local da ocorrência para atendimento das vítimas e identificou que ele morreu ainda no local. Outra vítima que estava no mesmo veículo foi atendida e encaminhada para o Hospital Regional de Sorriso .

O condutor da carreta não se feriu e assinou o termo de recusa de encaminhamento médico.

A perícia foi acionada e realizou os procedimentos necessários no local. Com a conclusão, o guincho da Nova Rota realizou a remoção dos veículos. O tráfego seguiu parcialmente interditado durante os atendimentos, sendo completamente liberado às 0h08.

articles.title: Jovem que morreu em cachoeira de Penedo ficou 16 minutos sem oxigênio | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente aconteceu no poço Três Cachoeiras; vítima foi identificada como Bruno Xavier, morador de Barra Mansa; segundo o Samu ele não resistiu às manobras de reanimação; corpo foi levado ao IML de Volta Redonda.
articles.summary: Acidente aconteceu no poço Três Cachoeiras; vítima foi identificada como Bruno Xavier; segundo o Samu ele não resistiu às manobras de reanimação.
articles.body:
Vítima que morreu afogada em Penedo foi identificada como Bruno Xavier, morador de Barra Mansa (RJ). — Foto: Divulgação/Redes sociais

O jovem, de 24 anos, que morreu afogado no domingo (30) ficou cerca de 4 minutos preso sob a água e 16 minutos sem oxigênio no poço Três Cachoeiras, na Avenida das Três Cachoeiras, no distrito de Penedo, em Itatiaia (RJ). A vítima foi identificada como Bruno Xavier, morador de Barra Mansa (RJ).

De acordo com o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu), a central recebeu o chamado às 16h13. A equipe registrou que o jovem ficou preso em uma cavidade debaixo d'água por cerca de 4 minutos antes de ser retirado.

Ainda segundo o Samu, durante o deslocamento da ambulância, a médica reguladora da central orientou por telefone que populares iniciassem manobras de reanimação cardiopulmonar.

Uma agente da Guarda Municipal que patrulhava a região também foi ao local ao ser alertada por testemunhas. A equipe de suporte básico do Samu chegou às 16h24 e assumiu o atendimento, utilizando um Desfibrilador Externo Automático (DEA) e manta térmica, mas a vítima não respondeu aos estímulos, ficou sem oxigênio por cerca de 16 minutos e teve o óbito foi constatado ainda no local.

Equipes das polícias Militar e Civil acompanharam a ocorrência. A área foi preservada para a perícia e o corpo foi removido para o Instituto Médico Legal (IML) de Volta Redonda (RJ). O caso foi registrado na delegacia de Itatiaia.

O g1 apura as informações sobre o velório e sepultamento.

articles.title: Hospital em Óbidos realiza 180 atendimentos de saúde pelo SUS | G1
articles.standfirst: Consultas e exames foram realizados no Hospital Dom Floriano por meio de parceria entre o governo do estado e a Santa Casa de Misericórdia
articles.summary: O Hospital em Óbidos realizou consultas de ortopedia e ultrassom pelo SUS em parceria com o governo do Pará e a Santa Casa de Misericórdia.
articles.body:
Hospital Dom Floriano, em Óbidos. — Foto: Ascom

O Hospital Dom Floriano, em Óbidos , no oeste do Pará, encerra nesta segunda-feira (31) uma ação de saúde que ofereceu mais de 180 atendimentos gratuitos para usuários do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS). O mutirão incluiu mais de 60 consultas de ortopedia e 120 exames de ultrassonografia.

Os atendimentos começaram no sábado (29) com as consultas ortopédicas. Já os exames de ultrassom foram realizados no domingo (30) e nesta segunda. Todos os procedimentos foram conduzidos pelo médico Juliano Citra.

A iniciativa é fruto de uma parceria entre o Governo do Pará, por meio da Secretaria de Estado de Saúde (Sespa), e a Associação de Caridade Santa Casa de Misericórdia de Óbidos, que administra o hospital. O objetivo do convênio é ampliar a oferta de serviços médicos de média e alta complexidade na região do Baixo Amazonas.

O Hospital Dom Floriano é mantido pela Santa Casa de Misericórdia de Óbidos, uma instituição filantrópica centenária.

A mobilização da comunidade para construir o hospital começou em 1920, com o objetivo de garantir cirurgias, internações e partos para a população local. A Associação de Caridade foi fundada oficialmente em 7 de setembro de 1922, durante as comemorações do Centenário da Independência do Brasil.

Atualmente, a parceria com o governo estadual ajuda a manter e expandir os atendimentos especializados para os moradores da região.

articles.title: California mom has both legs amputated after suspected impaired driver plows into her restaurant lunch table
articles.summary: A California woman underwent three surgeries and a bilateral leg amputation after an alleged impaired driver crashed into a Boyle Heights restaurant.
articles.body: An elderly California mother had both her legs amputated after an alleged impaired driver crashed into the outdoor dining area of a restaurant where she was eating lunch. Cristina Vargas, 81, was enjoying lunch at a sidewalk table outside Los Cinco Puntos in Los Angeles' Boyle Heights with her daughter, Gabriela Vargas, and their male friend when the SUV plowed into them at around 3:30 p.m. on July 7. Surveillance footage obtained by KTLA shows an SUV veering onto the sidewalk and into the outdoor dining area. Screeching tires were heard just before the SUV hit the group, sending patrons, the table and other items flying. ARIZONA GRANDPA TO UNDRGO AMPUTATION AFTER COLLAPSING ON SCORCHING SIDEWALK "I remember I just heard screeching and I was lifting up my head and I just saw headlights and a bumper and I heard a big boom," Gabriela told KTLA. "The next thing I knew, I was airborne." Cristina’s lower body was pinned under the vehicle and Gabriela suffered a head injury and a deep laceration on her knee. The two women and their male friend were rushed to a hospital for treatment. Gabriela and the male friend have since recovered from their injuries, but Cristina's injuries were significantly worse and faces a long road to recovery. Cristina underwent three surgeries and later had both of her legs amputated. She said she is thankful to be alive and has maintained a positive mindset. She has been undergoing physical therapy at a rehabilitation center and will soon be allowed to go back home. Cristina, a widowed mother of two, said she is looking forward to being surrounded by her family and friends. "My goal is to give her the best quality of care from here on out," Gabriela said of her mother. A police report alleges that the driver was impaired at the time of the crash. The unidentified woman was arrested and charged with multiple felonies, according to KTLA. A GoFundMe created by a friend for the Vargas family has raised more than $30,000 as of Sunday night. The fundraiser said the family is facing massive medical bills, ongoing rehabilitation and daily living expenses. "Cristina will need significant support to adapt to her new disability, including making their home accessible and covering the costs of specialized care. The road ahead is long and challenging, but with your help, they can focus on healing rather than the overwhelming financial stress," the fundraiser reads. CALIFORNIA MAN PICKS UP EXPLOSIVE DEVICE ON A BEACH DURING JULY 4 CLEANUP, LOSES HAND CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The fundraiser described Cristina as a "vibrant and social person with a true lust for life." "She loved to dance and was a regular at events at the senior center, bringing joy and energy wherever she went," the GoFundMe reads. "Her vivacious spirit and love for connecting with others made her a beloved member of the community. This sudden change is especially heartbreaking for someone who has always embraced life so fully and actively." In an Aug. 17 update, Gabriela thanked supporters and said the recovery was progressing slowly. "Thank you everybody for your love and support. We greatly appreciate it. It's a slow recovery but day by day we're getting through it. My mom's spirits remain hopeful as do mine. Recovery is very painful but she's giving it her all," Gabriela said.

articles.title: Tunisia swelters as power cuts disrupt water supplies
articles.summary: Near 50C temperatures are driving record electricity demand, disrupting water supplies and straining health services.
articles.body:
Tunisia is facing another spell of extreme heat, with temperatures reaching 49.8 degrees Celsius (121.6 Fahrenheit) in the central city of Kairouan on August 27.

The heat has coincided with electricity cuts and water shortages in parts of the country, while doctors have warned of mounting pressure on emergency departments.

The electricity and water disruptions are linked in some areas, but they have different underlying causes.

Kairouan reached 49.8°C on August 27, according to the Tunisian Observatory for Weather and Climate. The observatory said Kairouan was the second-hottest location among those monitored worldwide that day, behind Mehran in Iran, which reached 50°C. Six Tunisian cities were among the world’s 20 hottest monitoring stations.

The reading was also close to Tunisia’s national temperature record of 50.3°C, recorded on August 11, 2021.

The extreme temperatures have pushed up electricity demand as households and businesses use more air conditioning. Water demand also rises during periods of extreme heat, adding pressure to a system already facing longer-term shortages.

The Tunisian Company of Electricity and Gas (STEG) has introduced rotating power cuts in several regions.

The immediate pressure on the electricity system has come from exceptionally high demand during periods of extreme heat, particularly because of heavy use of air conditioning.

STEG officials said electricity demand may have reached a record 6,000 megawatts in July, after reaching 5,600MW only days earlier.

STEG has said the rotating cuts are intended to protect the safety and continuity of the electricity system.

The outages have affected areas across Tunisia rather than a single region.

STEG has introduced temporary cuts in several parts of the country as it manages pressure on the network. The timing and duration have varied, with some residents reporting interruptions lasting several hours.

Parts of Tunisia’s water-distribution system depend on electrically powered pumping stations. When electricity is interrupted, those stations can stop operating, disrupting the movement and distribution of water.

There is a clear recent example. On August 24, an electricity interruption stopped the main Kerker pumping station, disrupting drinking-water supplies in several areas of the Mahdia and Sfax governorates, according to Tunisia’s National Company for Water Exploitation and Distribution (SONEDE).

The incident shows how a disruption to electricity at a pumping station can quickly affect water supplies.

But that does not mean every water shortage is caused by a power cut.

Was Tunisia already facing water shortages?

Yes. Tunisia has been dealing with structural water scarcity and recurring drought for years. The World Bank describes the country as facing growing water scarcity and climate pressures and is supporting projects to improve the reliability and resilience of drinking-water services.

The current electricity cuts are therefore adding pressure to an existing water problem rather than creating Tunisia’s water crisis from scratch.

Water interruptions can have several causes, including shortages, infrastructure problems, maintenance and disruptions to pumping and distribution.

What is happening to bottled-water supplies?

The heat and electricity disruptions have also affected bottled-water supplies.

The Associated Press reported that power rationing disrupted factory operations as demand for bottled water increased during the heatwave. Production was also affected by shortages of raw plastic materials.

The shortage therefore cannot be attributed to electricity cuts alone.

What does a power cut mean for households?

During a heatwave, losing electricity means more than losing lights.

Air conditioners and fans stop working. Refrigerators and freezers stop cooling. If an outage lasts for several hours, households may struggle to keep perishable food safely refrigerated.

For businesses, prolonged outages can mean lost refrigerated stock and disrupted operations.

And when a power interruption affects water-pumping infrastructure, households can face two basic-service disruptions at once: less electricity and less reliable access to water.

The heat is also putting pressure on emergency departments.

On August 29, the Tunisian Organization of Young Doctors said emergency departments were experiencing an “unprecedented” increase in deaths and hospital admissions associated with heatstroke and extreme temperatures.

The organisation called for the government to declare a health emergency and said doctors and nurses were under severe pressure.

Wajih Dhakkar, head of the organisation, said 13 people had died within 24 hours at Habib Bourguiba Hospital in Sfax.

That figure comes from the doctors’ organisation and is not an official nationwide death toll.

The Health Ministry said on August 29 that 633 cases requiring medical consultation and healthcare management related to the effects of the heatwave had been recorded between July 1 and August 29. It also said health services had continued without interruption and that medical and technical resources had been mobilised.

The ministry did not provide a nationwide death toll.

What about patients who depend on electricity?

Power cuts can create particular difficulties for people who rely on electricity-dependent medical equipment at home.

Oxygen concentrators, for example, require electricity to operate.

There have been reports in Tunisia of difficulties for patients whose home medical equipment was affected by electricity interruptions. But individual deaths attributed directly to a power cut require confirmation from medical professionals or authorities.

There is also not enough reliable evidence to say that surgeries across Tunisia are being cancelled because of the electricity cuts.

Is the heat the only reason for the electricity and water problems?

No. The heat has sharply increased electricity demand, particularly because of air-conditioning use. That has put additional pressure on the electricity network.

But Tunisia’s water problems predate the current heatwave. The country faces structural water scarcity, drought and infrastructure challenges.

Water interruptions can therefore have several causes, including shortages, infrastructure problems, maintenance and disruptions to pumping and distribution.

President Kais Saied has offered another explanation for some of the recent disruptions.

On August 27, Saied said investigations had shown that water and electricity disruptions were not the result of routine technical failures but rather what he described as deliberate acts of sabotage intended to stir tensions and spread rumours. He did not identify those he said were responsible.

That remains the president’s claim and should not be presented as an established explanation for the outages as a whole.

There are documented technical explanations for at least some disruptions. STEG has said its temporary electricity cuts are intended to protect the stability and continuity of the power system, while SONEDE has documented a case in which an electricity interruption stopped a water-pumping station.

Repeated interruptions to electricity and water have added to public frustration and have become a focus of protests against the government.

A protest in Tunis organised by the Nafas movement on August 20 included demands for better access to water and electricity, alongside concerns over living costs and political freedoms.

For households, the immediate impact is practical: a power cut during extreme heat means no air conditioning and less reliable refrigeration. If the interruption affects a pumping station, it can also mean less water.

For some patients, it can create difficulties if they depend on electricity-powered equipment.

As long as temperatures remain high, electricity demand is likely to remain elevated, particularly while households and businesses rely heavily on air conditioning.

That keeps pressure on the electricity network. Further power cuts could affect water pumping, refrigeration and electricity-dependent medical equipment.

The current crisis shows how closely Tunisia’s electricity and water systems can be linked — but also why they should not be treated as the same problem.

Extreme heat is putting immediate pressure on the electricity network. Power cuts can then disrupt parts of the water system. But Tunisia’s underlying water crisis is older and broader, rooted in long-term water scarcity and infrastructure challenges.

articles.title: Statins and dementia: Cholesterol-lowering drugs may cut dementia risk by 15%, study finds
articles.summary: Wellness News: Many of us are already well aware of statins being everywhere in the world of heart health. But it turns out their story might not end with arteries a.
articles.body: Many of us are already well aware of statins being everywhere in the world of heart health. But it turns out their story might not end with arteries and cholesterol. A major Danish study just shed some fresh light on these common drugs. People who began taking statins shortly after learning they had type 2 diabetes seemed to have a smaller chance of developing dementia over the next decade compared to those who skipped or delayed the pills.The researchers published the study in The Lancet Regional Health – Europe and talked about it at the European Society of Cardiology Congress 2026. Now, here’s why this matters: both type 2 diabetes and high LDL (“bad”) cholesterol are well-known troublemakers. They don’t just raise the risk of heart attacks or strokes; they’re also linked to worsening thinking and memory as people get older.According to this study, starting statins within that crucial first year after a diabetes diagnosis led to a 15% dip in relative risk for dementia over 10 years. Even people who started later (within five years) saw a 10% reduction.But before anyone starts celebrating, let’s be clear: this research doesn’t prove statins prevent dementia. The scientists watched what happened to people over time, rather than giving everyone the same treatment and watching for differences. In the research world, that means you can find patterns and associations, but you can’t say statins are the smoking gun that keeps dementia at bay.What did they actually look at, and what did they learn?For starters, the study tracked over 132,000 people. This wasn’t a tiny trial; they dug into the health records of 132,585 people in Denmark who developed type 2 diabetes from 2006 to 2019. None had taken statins before. Researchers split everyone into three groups: some never started statins during the first five years, others began within a year, and the rest started between one and five years after diagnosis. Then they followed each person until they either developed dementia, died, moved, or until the calendar hit the end of 2021.Here’s what happened:Over a typical follow-up period of about seven years, just under 3% (3,592 people) ended up with dementia.Crunching the numbers over a 10-year stretch, people who didn’t start statins saw nearly a 4% risk of developing dementia (3.9% to be precise). Early starters had a risk of 3.3%, while those who began later saw 3.5%.So, in relative terms? That’s a 15% reduction for those who got statins right away, and 10% for those who waited a bit.Why might statins help the brain, and not just the heart?Let’s zoom out a bit. Statins are already best known for lowering LDL cholesterol, which creates fatty deposits in blood vessels. Blocked or narrowed vessels can eventually mean heart attacks or strokes. But brains need healthy blood flow, too.Things get more complicated in the brain. Diabetes itself is a red flag for cognitive problems. And when blood vessels throughout the body get damaged, that harm may contribute to types of dementia, especially vascular dementia, and make things worse for brains already at risk for Alzheimer’s disease. The researchers suspect that lowering LDL with statins early in the diabetes journey might protect those tiny, vulnerable vessels inside the brain.Now, this is a theory. While it fits what we know so far, the new data doesn’t prove that’s the real explanation for the dementia drop.The timing seems to make the most differenceThe crucial bit one needs to pay attention to? Timing matters. According to this study, taking statins within the first year after a type 2 diabetes diagnosis makes a bigger difference for dementia risk than waiting a few years. The relative benefits break down like this: a 15% risk reduction with early statins, 10% if treatment starts later on.In real terms, the head start isn’t dramatic. If you look at 100 people, early statin takers avoided about half a case of dementia, or 0.59 percentage points, over 10 years compared to non-users. Those who delayed statins saw a smaller benefit (about 0.38 points lower risk compared to non-users).Notably, both men and women seemed to benefit in roughly the same way.Most people with diabetes are already prescribed statins for their heartDon’t count on doctors changing course or prescribing statins just to ward off dementia. People with diabetes are already high on the list to receive statins, simply because they face a much bigger risk of heart trouble. The American Diabetes Association recommends that pretty much everyone with diabetes between 40 and 75 should be on at least a moderate dose of statins, unless they already have serious heart disease.The main reason will always be to protect the heart and blood vessels: a reduction in heart attacks, strokes, and complications tied to high cholesterol. Any dementia-related benefit is still being explored and isn’t the leading reason to take statins right now.Do statins really stop dementia?It’s not a slam dunk yet. The study stopped short of claiming statins directly ward off dementia. People who choose to start early might have healthier habits, easier access to healthcare, or be more proactive about their health than those who don’t. There’s just no way to perfectly control for all those differences in an observational study.We need randomized clinical trials, which are the gold standard for proving cause and effect, before anyone can say for sure whether statins protect the brain. The authors and the European Society of Cardiology both urge caution: don’t read this as definitive proof.But the evidence does fit into a larger story. Look across other studies, and you’ll find a similar suggestion: healthy blood vessels support a healthy brain. Past research has even hinted at links between statin use and a lower risk for Alzheimer’s, but the results swing back and forth depending on the study.What’s the bottom line?If you have type 2 diabetes and your healthcare provider suggests a statin for heart health, don’t wait around. Start it promptly, and you may be giving your brain a bonus, too. But hold off on taking statins solely to prevent dementia. Talk it over with your doctor, stick to the tried-and-true reasons for cholesterol-lowering medication, and pay attention as researchers keep digging.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: The dance group helping with addiction and mental health issues
articles.summary: The dancers are preparing to perform a sold-out show at the Royal Opera House in London.
articles.body:
In a studio in Chester, dancers are finessing the choreography for their forthcoming sold-out performance at the Royal Opera House in London.

While they have all bonded over a shared love of dancing, they have also overcome similar struggles to get here.

"We've all been through trauma and our own journey," explained Michelle Hughes.

Fallen Angels Dance Theatre was set up to help provide an outlet both for people in recovery from addiction and those who have struggled with their mental health.

Through dancing, it wants to help participants transform their lives and share their recovery journeys.

Michelle, who has been a member since 2021, was aware of the group as part of her work as an alcohol misuse engagement worker at the Countess of Chester Hospital.

But she said she started coming to the sessions for her "own needs" after fracturing her skull in a fall and suffering two family bereavements in close succession.

"It has really helped," she said. "I'm a recovering alcoholic, nearly 16 years now.

"I didn't want to turn to drink, which why I came to the group for myself.

"The group is fantastic. As I'm severely visually impaired, people are really supportive and help me."

Tom Denbigh has been coming to the dance classes for seven years after being diagnosed with PTSD from his childhood.

He is also no stranger to this environment, having met his wife at ballroom dancing.

Tom admitted too that he is always the first one on the dance floor at weddings.

"What surprised me is the emotion I felt when I first went," said the 77-year-old from Bromborough on Merseyside.

"At my first session I was virtually in tears all the way through it because of some emotion it had brought up."

Hayden Etienne, from Liscard on Merseyside, joined the group three years ago after suffering with anxiety, panic attacks and depression.

The 66-year-old said the group had opened doors to meet other people who had faced similar struggles.

"I meet regularly with like-minded souls – people who have had their own journey so there is no ego there," he said.

Claire Morris, who is the creative and strategic director at Fallen Angels Dance Theatre, said the project enabled its members to create "a memory that will last a lifetime".

"If you've had those challenges in your life then your mind can be very busy, very distracted and very conflicting," she said.

"But you come to Fallen Angels and you get out of your mind and into your body and it just releases all those tensions and all those worries of the week."

The group will perform Holding Light - choreographed by Russell Maliphant - at London's Royal Opera House in September, followed by performances at Chester's Storyhouse and Liverpool's Everyman Theatre.

articles.title: Dante Dionisi, entrenador y profesor de educación física: "Si no puedes correr, existen otros ejercicios para ti..."
articles.standfirst: Las personas con movilidad reducida tienen opciones muy beneficiosas también
articles.summary: Las personas con movilidad reducida tienen opciones muy beneficiosas también
articles.body: A la hora de ponernos en forma o tener una vida activa, muchas veces se nos va la mente a deportes tan sencillos y efectivos como caminar o salir a correr. Sin embargo, muchas personas tienen condiciones o cualidades diversas que les limitan para poder practicarlo y, las opciones para tener una vida activa y saludable a nivel físico, se reducen. Por ello, el entrenador y profesor de educación física Dante Dionisi, ha publicado en sus redes sociales un reel en el que recomienda ejercicios para personas con movilidad reducida, muy sencillos de realizar y con poco material para ponerlos en práctica. Uno de los ejercicios que muestra el especialista empieza sentado en una silla. Con los pies apoyados en el suelo, recomienda levantar los talones y bajarlos de forma repetida para movilizar los tobillos, pies y gemelos. El segundo ejercicio que recomienda es idóneo para la movilidad y la coordinación, aunque es más complejo que el anterior. Para este ejercicio empezamos de la misma manera, sentados en la silla y con los pies apoyados en el suelo; aunque debes poner los brazos extendidos a la altura de tus ojos y sostener una pica de madera o plástico. El gesto que debemos hacer en este ejercicio es mover la pica hacia el pecho y hacia adelante y, con cada uno de estos movimientos, levantar y bajar las piernas de forma alterna. El tercer ejercicio es similar al segundo, pero debes empezar separando un poco más las piernas. La pica esta vez, se moverá al son de tu tronco, y deberás sostener la pica con los brazos al frente y girar el tronco para movilizarlo y ejercitarlo. El ejercicio es fundamental y se convierte en una pieza clave para cualquier persona. Si además te ves limitado por tu movilidad reducida, se convierte en una actividad necesaria y vitalizante. Sin embargo, no solo es importante incorporar estas actividades, sino que es necesario poner en práctica otras actividades estimulantes y positivas. Una de las recomendadas por los expertos son los juegos de mesa, casi de cualquier tipo. Ayudan a mejorar y entrenar la mente, así como fomentar la paciencia. Cuestiones fundamentales para casi cualquier persona. Además, al tener un menor rango de movilidad, es necesario que se cuide la alimentación para evitar el sobrepeso y prevenir problemas comunes como el estreñimiento. Todo ello sin descuidar la hidratación que puede ayudar a cuidar los riñones y la piel, entre otras cuestiones.

articles.title: Minnie Merriman: Mum thanks public for 'incredible' support
articles.summary: The nine-year-old died earlier this month after being found seriously injured in Arbroath.
articles.body:
The mother of a nine-year-old girl who died after being found seriously injured in Arbroath has thanked people in the town for their "incredible support."

Minnie Merriman, from Wakefield, West Yorkshire, died in hospital in Dundee following an incident at Elliot Industrial Estate on 3 August.

Minnie's father Christopher Rice is accused of murdering his daughter and is currently remanded in custody ahead of a trial.

In a Facebook post, Laurie Merriman said the generosity shown by local people had been "overwhelming" and meant "more to us than we could ever put into words".

Hundreds pay tribute to Minnie Merriman in Arbroath

Family 'overwhelmed' after Arbroath FC hold silence for Minnie Merriman

The post included a photo of Laurie and Minnie at Arbroath Cliffs.

Laurie said: "I want to thank you wholeheartedly for the incredible love and support you have shown me and my beautiful Minnie during the worst time of my life.

"The humanity and kindness carries me and will be with me every step of the way in my fight for justice for my Minnie."

Hundreds of people gathered in Arbroath's Victoria Park last week to pay their respects to Minnie.

A private ambulance carrying Minnie's body home to England was accompanied by a motorcycle escort to the park.

Local people laid flowers, poems and toys beside the private ambulance.

Following the event, which saw balloons being released, a piper led a procession accompanied by Minnie's family.

Laurie added: "To every person who came out for Minnie's journey home, every biker, neighbour and stranger who stood with us - thank you.

"To the football club for your support and the Arbroath shirts for Minnie's little brothers, the family who gave us a place to stay when we needed it most, and for the giant chocolate gifts that brought a smile to the boys' little faces.

She also thanked everyone who had donated and "helped raise money in Minnie's name".

The town previously paid tribute to Minnie with a minutes' silence before Arbroath's match against Inverness Caledonian Thistle on 8 August.

Emergency services were called to the Elliot Industrial Estate in Arbroath shortly after midnight on 3 August following reports that a child had been found injured.

Minnie was taken to Ninewells Hospital along with four other people, but later died as a result of her injuries.

articles.title: Dietitian reveals simple eating strategy for better sleep — and one habit to avoid
articles.summary: Tart cherry juice tops a dietitian's list of sleep-boosting foods, with its natural melatonin content shown to improve both sleep quality and quantity.
articles.body: How you eat can influence how you sleep, according to experts. Erin Palinski-Wade, a New Jersey-based registered dietitian, certified diabetes care specialist and author of "The Sleepdemic Solution," says certain foods can make, or break, a good night’s sleep. "There are a number of foods that can help support sleep, and sometimes it's even a combination," she told Fox News Digital. 5-STEP SLEEP RESET COULD PROMOTE HEALTHY WEIGHT LOSS, NUTRITIONIST SAYS Supporting better sleep Keeping blood sugar steady throughout the day may help prevent afternoon energy crashes and support more restorative sleep at night, Palinski-Wade said. Waking up in the middle of the night and struggling to fall back asleep may not always be insomnia, she suggested, but could be linked to fluctuations in glucose levels. Combining lean proteins, slow-digesting carbohydrates and healthy fats in meals and snacks can help stabilize those levels — what Palinski-Wade called the "No. 1 way" to improve overall sleep. Some small studies suggest tart cherry juice may support sleep, and the expert named tart cherries — or 100% tart cherry juice — as her top choice. FOOD CRAVINGS AT 3:45 PM AREN'T RANDOM, HERE'S WHAT YOUR BODY MAY BE WARNING YOU ABOUT "Tart cherries [are] one of the foods that have the highest amount of melatonin naturally, but they also have compounds that help to really extend that melatonin in our bodies and our body's ability to use it," she said. Still, research linking tart cherry consumption to modest improvements in sleep duration or quality is limited and mixed; a 2025 systematic review reached a similar conclusion. For those who suffer from insomnia, Palinski-Wade recommends ingesting 4 to 6 ounces of 100% tart cherry juice, or about a quarter cup of dried tart cherries. "It's a really, really great tool to improve your sleep – and it's really tasty, too," she said. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Foods and drinks that may help reduce inflammation can also support sleep, the dietitian said. "When we have more antioxidants in the body, more anti-inflammatory compounds, we're really helping our body to achieve that more restful state," Palinski-Wade said. Foods rich in antioxidants and anti-inflammatory compounds — including nuts and seeds, olive oil and avocados — also provide healthy fats and other nutrients that may support sleep. Caffeine’s sleep impact On the other hand, Palinski-Wade warned that caffeine intake can negatively impact sleep quality. "So many of us have a poor night's sleep and the next day we reach for caffeine to give us a burst of energy," she said. "And there's nothing wrong with a little bit of caffeine, but you have to look at how much you're having and how close to bedtime." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "And it's a stimulant, so it's harder to fall asleep," Palinski-Wade warned. "If you have foods or beverages with a large amount of caffeine, and you're having them in the afternoon or toward the evening, that is going to make it very hard to get restorative, restful sleep in the evening." For those who do drink caffeine, it is best to stop about 10 hours before bedtime, the expert advised. The "sweet spot" for daily caffeine intake is 300 milligrams or less, she said. Any more than that becomes a "stressor to our body." A cup of coffee, traditionally 8 ounces, is about 100 milligrams. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES The FDA says up to 400 milligrams daily is not generally associated with negative effects for most adults, although individual tolerance can vary depending on factors such as medications, health conditions and sensitivity to caffeine. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "We start to release stress hormones like cortisol and adrenaline, and that not only makes our body store fat versus burn it, but it also increases inflammation," Palinski-Wade noted. "So now you have the stimulant, you have this inflammation, and all those things go against quality sleep."

articles.title: Israeli air strikes on Gaza kill at least five people: Report
articles.summary: Israel escalates its attacks across the Gaza Strip in recent days despite a US-brokered ‘ceasefire’.
articles.body:
Israeli attacks across Gaza have killed ⁠at least five people, according to health officials.

Medics said on Monday that two people were killed when an Israeli air strike hit a crowd near ⁠a municipal public park in Gaza City, an area packed with displaced families. Several people were reported to have been wounded.

A separate air strike hit a vehicle in the Tal al-Hawa neighbourhood in western Gaza City, killing at least three people, health officials said.

The Israeli military claimed the two attacks targeted Hamas fighters ‌without providing evidence.

Relatives and friends paid their respects to two of the five men killed on Monday at al-Shifa Hospital, Gaza’s largest medical facility, before carrying their bodies to a cemetery to bury them.

Israel has escalated its attacks across the Gaza Strip in recent days despite a “ceasefire” agreed in October. An Israeli strike on Deir el-Balah in central Gaza on Sunday killed two Palestinians, including a three-year-old, while Israeli attacks killed at least four people on Saturday.

“There is no ceasefire. There has not been one good day in Gaza since October 7, [2023],” Amjad Abu Abdo, a relative of one of the people killed in the attacks on Monday, told the Reuters news agency. “I swear, we do not sleep from ⁠the sound of drones. You sleep scared of being hit.”

Since the “ceasefire” between Israel and Hamas took effect, 1,313 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli attacks on Gaza, Gaza’s Ministry of Health said.

Meanwhile, 4,000 to 5,000 Palestinians remain missing and are believed to be dead under rubble in Gaza, the Palestinian Centre for Missing and Forcibly Disappeared Persons said on Saturday.

The Israeli army reported five deaths in its ranks since October as well as the death of one civilian contractor.

Since Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza began in October 2023, nearly 73,500 Palestinians have been confirmed killed in Gaza and nearly 174,500 injured, most of them women and children, according to the Health Ministry.

articles.title: Fake Chrome update scam could infect your computer
articles.summary: A Chrome extension with 70,000 users and a 4.7-star rating began injecting fake update warnings after a threat actor acquired and weaponized it.
articles.body: You are browsing the web when a warning suddenly takes over the page. It says your browser needs a "Critical Update" before you can continue. It looks like Chrome. The message feels urgent. So, clicking Update may seem like the safest thing you can do. That is exactly what makes this fake Chrome update scam so convincing. Recent reports linked aggressive fake browser update warnings to a Chrome extension called Enable Right Click & Copy - Smart Unlock + OCR. The extension was originally developed as a legitimate tool for restoring right-click and copying features on websites that block them. However, security researchers at Socket now say the extension was later acquired by a threat actor and updated with malicious functionality. It had around 70,000 users when that malicious functionality appeared, although researchers caution that this does not mean every user received the malicious version. The extension was delisted from the Chrome Web Store on Aug. 14 after being flagged as potentially malicious. FAKE WINDOWS UPDATE INSTALLS HIDDEN MALWARE The bigger lesson goes beyond one extension. Something you installed months ago and trusted every day can change after an update. Here's how this fake Chrome update scam works, how to spot the warning signs and what you can do to protect your browser and computer. Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our financial protection checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed. Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com. How the fake Chrome update scam works The warning can appear while you are visiting an otherwise normal website. You may see language such as "Critical Update Required" or "Update available." The alert then pushes you to download something before you continue browsing. However, Chrome normally handles its updates through the browser itself. Google says Chrome usually updates automatically in the background. You can also check manually by opening Chrome and going to More > Help > About Google Chrome. A webpage asking you to download a .vbs script or an unfamiliar .exe file to update Chrome should immediately raise your suspicion. Google specifically advises users to avoid suspicious pop-ups asking them to install updates. Instead, Google recommends going directly to the program or its official website. Why a trusted extension can suddenly become dangerous Here is the part that can catch careful people off guard. You may have installed an extension when it had thousands of users, strong reviews and no obvious signs of trouble. You use it for months. Then the extension changes. Google confirmed to CyberGuy that it looked into Enable Right Click & Copy - Smart Unlock + OCR. "We've investigated the extension and taken action to protect our users," a Google spokesperson told CyberGuy. New research published by Socket on Aug. 27 shows the threat went beyond fake update warnings. Researchers linked the extension to a larger campaign involving 19 Chrome and Edge extensions capable of delivering malicious payloads. Those capabilities included credential theft, cryptocurrency wallet draining, injected phishing pages and fake browser update lures. Socket says some of the extensions began as legitimate products before being acquired and weaponized by the threat actor. We have seen that pattern before. Earlier this year, researchers found that QuickLens - Search Screen with Google Lens changed ownership before a malicious update arrived. The extension had previously earned a Featured badge from Google. Researchers later found malicious functionality capable of injecting code, displaying fake Google update prompts and targeting sensitive information. Google removed QuickLens from the Chrome Web Store. CyberGuy has also reported on trusted browser extensions that later became spyware. One campaign affected 4.3 million users after extensions that began as useful tools eventually received malicious updates. That history changes how I look at browser extensions. A great rating tells you what people thought when they reviewed an extension. It cannot guarantee what a future update will do. Why the 4.7-star rating should get your attention This recent extension case had another detail I think everyone should notice. Enable Right Click & Copy - Smart Unlock + OCR still had an average rating near 4.7 stars as reports of the fake update warnings appeared. That can happen because thousands of earlier positive ratings remain part of the overall score. Meanwhile, recent reviews can begin filling with warnings. In this case, August reviews accused the extension of injecting fake Chrome update alerts. Several users said removing or disabling it stopped the prompts. So, before installing an extension, look beyond the overall star rating. Read the newest reviews as well. CyberGuy previously covered another browser-extension scam involving a fake ad blocker. That extension created computer problems and then tried to convince users to run dangerous commands to fix them. Why antivirus software may not immediately explain the problem One Reddit user who encountered the recent fake update warnings said a full scan found nothing. The user later traced the pop-ups to the Right Click extension. A clean scan should never convince you that a suspicious browser warning is safe. The extension itself may be creating or injecting what you see inside the browser. Meanwhile, a downloaded malicious file may pose a separate threat if you open or execute it. Google's Safe Browsing system checks installed extensions and downloads against known threats. Chrome can also disable extensions that Google identifies as malicious. Still, newly emerging threats can create a window where users encounter trouble before defenses catch up. That is why your own reaction to a suspicious prompt remains important. FAKE CAPTCHA SCAM CAN HACK YOUR COMPUTER This can happen outside Google Chrome Seeing a Chrome-branded warning inside another browser gives you a pretty good clue that something is wrong. Users of Chromium-based browsers including Brave and Opera have reported similar fake Chrome update prompts. Users connected those warnings with suspicious browser extensions rather than genuine browser updates. That makes sense because Chromium-based browsers can support many of the same types of browser extensions. If Opera suddenly tells you that Google Chrome desperately needs an update, do not follow the prompt. How to check whether Chrome really needs an update You never need to trust a random webpage to tell you whether Chrome needs updating. On your computer: Open Chrome > click the three-dot menu > Help > About Google Chrome. Chrome will check for available updates on that page. If an update has already been downloaded, you may see an option to relaunch Chrome. If you do not see Relaunch, Google says you are running the latest available version. That simple check can take much of the guesswork out of a scary update warning. How to remove a suspicious Chrome extension Look carefully at what you have installed. Google lets you turn an extension off temporarily or remove it completely. You can also open an extension's details and review whether it can read or change data on every website you visit. If you have Enable Right Click & Copy - Smart Unlock + OCR installed, I would remove it even if you never clicked or opened one of the suspicious downloads. Researchers found malicious capabilities that went beyond the fake update prompts. Then restart Chrome, run a full security scan and change passwords for sensitive accounts you used while the extension was installed from another trusted device. If you have several unfamiliar extensions, disable them and re-enable only the ones you recognize and still need. For more help identifying warning signs, CyberGuy has a full guide explaining how to tell if your browser has been hijacked. How to stay safe from fake Chrome update scams A few smart habits can lower your chances of turning a convincing pop-up into a serious security problem. 1) Never update Chrome from a webpage pop-up If a webpage tells you to download an update, close the warning. Then go directly to Chrome > Help > About Google Chrome. Google also warns people to use caution when websites claim you need to download software because your device has a virus. 2) Use strong antivirus software Strong antivirus protection adds another defense between a bad download and your computer. Look for antivirus software that provides real-time protection, rather than relying only on occasional manual scans. Real-time protection can monitor files as they arrive and look for suspicious behavior before malware gets a chance to spread. Keep the antivirus software updated as well. New threats appear constantly, so outdated security software can leave gaps. If you clicked a fake update or accidentally ran a suspicious file, perform a full system scan. Follow the antivirus program's instructions if it detects malware. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com. 3) Review your browser extensions regularly Take a minute every few months to see what you have installed. In Chrome on your computer: Pay particular attention to extensions that can read and change your data on all websites you visit. Google classifies access to data across all websites as a higher-risk permission because an extension may be able to read, request or modify information on pages you visit. If an extension suddenly asks for broader permissions or you no longer remember why you installed it, I would remove it. FAKE PARTY INVITATION SCAM CAN HIJACK YOUR COMPUTER 4) Read the newest reviews before installing Do not rely only on the overall rating. Scroll down and look at what people have written recently. A long history of five-star reviews can hide a sudden change that users discovered only days ago. If recent reviews suddenly mention pop-ups, malware or unexpected redirects, choose another extension. 5) Turn on Chrome's Enhanced Protection For additional protection, open: Chrome > Settings > Privacy and security > Security > Enhanced protection. Google says Enhanced Protection can warn you about potentially dangerous websites, downloads and extensions, including threats that Chrome has not previously identified. It also provides deeper checks on suspicious downloads. 6) Delete unexpected files without opening them If you clicked a fake update and it downloaded a .vbs, .exe or another unfamiliar file, do not open it. Delete it. Then empty your Recycle Bin or Trash and run a full security scan. Chrome may also block files it considers dangerous, suspicious or unverified. Treat those warnings seriously rather than overriding them to get the download through. 7) Use a data removal service to reduce your exposure A data removal service cannot remove malware from your computer. However, it can reduce another piece of the scammer's advantage: the amount of personal information about you that sits online. Data brokers can collect details such as contact information, previous addresses and other identifying information. Scammers can use exposed data to make follow-up phishing attempts feel much more believable. For example, a scammer who already knows your name, phone number and where you live has more material to personalize a fake security alert. Data removal services work by sending removal requests to data brokers and other sites that publish personal information. They can also continue checking whether your information reappears. Reducing that digital footprint will never stop every scam. However, giving criminals less information to work with can make targeted attacks harder to personalize. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com. Take extra precautions if you opened the downloaded file If you actually executed the suspicious file, treat the computer as potentially compromised. What to do if the fake Chrome update keeps appearing If you removed a suspicious extension and the warning still appears, continue narrowing down the cause. Kurt's key takeaways What bothers me most about this fake Chrome update scam is how little suspicious behavior it requires from the person being targeted. You could have downloaded a useful extension from the official Chrome Web Store. It could have worked exactly as promised. It could even have thousands of happy users. Then something changes behind the scenes. That means we need to stop treating browser extensions as install-once-and-forget-about-it utilities. Every extension gets a level of access to your browser. The fewer you keep around, the smaller that exposure becomes. I would also make one rule nonnegotiable: Never update Chrome because a webpage tells you to download a file. Open Chrome's settings and check the update yourself. That extra 20 seconds could save you from turning a convincing fake warning into a much bigger security headache. articles.title: Texas fire department makes save on crane 22 stories in the air
articles.summary: The Fort Worth Fire Department shared photos and detailed the rescue of an individual from the cab of a towering crane in the Lone Star State.
articles.body: Responders rescued an individual from the cab of a towering crane in Texas on Saturday, according to the Fort Worth Fire Department. The department detailed the save in a Saturday Facebook post, which noted that the individual was about 220 feet high. "The Fort Worth Fire Department Alarm Office received a call for a medical emergency at 11:50am today," the post noted, explaining, "The location was at... the construction site at JPS Health Hospital. Upon arrival, crews found that the patient was actually located approximately 220 feet up in the air, inside of a crane cab." Responders climbed up, provided medical aid and lowered the individual to the ground, the department noted. "When technical rescue teams arrived on scene, they gathered gear and began their ascent up the crane’s ladder. They carried with them all of the equipment they would need for the entire rescue on their backs," the department said. "Upon arrival at the top of the crane (over 22 stories in the air), they went to work. Immediate emergency medical care was started while technical rescue teams began devising a plan for the patient’s safe descent," the department continued. "Once the patient was safely hooked up to the ropes and rigging system, the crews had him lowered and on the ground. This all happened within less than an hour of their making it to him initially," the post read. The department shared multiple photos of the heroic rescue effort. articles.title: Popular artificial sweetener linked to potentially dangerous heart risk
articles.summary: A new study of over 17,700 participants links higher xylitol blood levels to increased cardiovascular risk, including heart attack and stroke, over future decades.
articles.body: People who consume greater amounts of a popular artificial sweetener could face a greater risk of heart attack and stroke, a new study suggests. The research, which was presented at the ESC Cardiology Congress in Germany this week, showed that higher levels of xylitol in the blood were associated with an increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Xylitol is a sugar alcohol that is commonly used as a low-calorie sweetener and sugar substitute, according to the National Institutes of Health. It is often used in higher amounts to sweeten foods, drinks, chewing gum and dental care products. ZERO-CALORIE SWEETENERS COULD ALTER THE GENES OF LATER GENERATIONS, NEW STUDY WARNS The researchers followed two large study cohorts of more than 17,700 Canadian and British participants. Over a six-year follow-up, people in the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging with the highest xylitol levels had a 57% higher risk of death, myocardial infarction or stroke related to cardiovascular events compared to those with the lowest levels. Over 30 years, participants in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer (EPIC)-Norfolk group with the highest xylitol levels had an 18% greater risk of MACE. Both cohorts showed evidence of a dose-dependent association, in which higher blood xylitol concentrations corresponded to higher rates of cardiovascular events. DIRTY SODA DRINKS ARE EVERYWHERE, BUT DOCTORS WARN OF HEALTH RISKS: 'METABOLIC DISASTER' These higher risks persisted even after the researchers adjusted for other factors like age, gender, body mass index, hypertension, diabetes and lipid levels. The study follows previous research that showed xylitol can enhance the ability of platelets to form clots, according to Dr. Marco Witkowski, the study presenter from Charité University Hospital in Berlin, Germany. "Artificial sweeteners are consumed by people who think they are healthier than sugar, and they are generally regarded as safe by regulatory agencies," the doctor said in a statement. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "Our long-term findings in the general population highlight how little we know about the cardiovascular safety of xylitol and indicate that further studies are warranted, especially as the amount of xylitol in products continues to increase." CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES The study was observational and does not prove that xylitol causes cardiovascular events, as the researchers noted that more studies are needed to confirm the findings. The report also does not establish whether high levels of xylitol in the blood necessarily reflect dietary consumption, as the sugar alcohol can also be produced naturally in the body as part of glucose metabolism. "These disturbing findings with [a] plausible mechanism of xylitol increasing cardiovascular risk should be taken very seriously," Dr. Aseem Malhotra, a cardiologist and public health campaigner based in London, told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "As a practicing cardiologist, I see many patients suffering from anxiety and palpitations that resolve as soon as they stop taking artificial sweeteners." Malhotra, who was not involved in the study, noted that one of the most important dietary changes to reduce cardiovascular risk is to "unsweeten your sweet tooth."
